 This Writ Petition Is Filed Under Articles 226 &
227 Of Constitution Of India, Praying To Issue
Directions To The Government To Issue De-
Notification In Respect Of 1 Acres 28 Guntas Land In
Sy. No.9 Situated At Somanakoppa Village, Kasaba
Hobli, Shimoga Taluk & District As Notification
Issued In The Case Of Madar Sab In Sy. No. 131,
Measuring 3 Acres 23 Gunts And Parameshwarappa In
Sy. No.16/2, Measuring 1 Acre 14 Gunts As Per
Annexure - 'A' And Etc.
 This Writ Petition Having Been Heard And
Reserved On 03.07.2023 And Coming On For
Pronouncement Of Orders, This Day, The Court Made
The Following:
 3
 Order

The petitioner has sought for issuance of order/directions to the Government to issue an order of de-notification in respect of an extent of 1 acre 28 guntas in Survey No.9 situated at Somanakoppa Village, Kasaba Hobli, Shivamogga Taluk and District, while extending the same benefit as extended in the case of Sri Madarsab in Survey No.131, measuring 3 acres 23 guntas and Sri Parameshwarappa in Survey No.16/2 measuring 1 acre 14 guntas, whose lands have been excluded.
2. The petitioner submits that he is the owner of the land measuring 7 acres 28 guntas in Survey No.9 in the Village referred hereinabove.
3. It is stated that the Preliminary Notification came to be passed on 12.11.1992, which was followed up by a Final Notification on 24.05.1994, which covered the land of the petitioner.

entities.text: V Gopalakrishna vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that there was a proposal of amicable settlement between the Urban Development Authority and the petitioner and it was agreed to return an extent of 1 acre 28 guntas of land bearing Survey No.9 to the petitioner and take possession of 6 acres.

It is further asserted that the Authority had paid compensation only to the extent of 6 acres of land in Survey No.9.
5.

It is stated that, though in the case of other land owners, i.e. Sri Madarsab and Sri Parameshwarappa, an order of de-notification came to be passed under Section 48(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the same benefit has not been extended to the petitioner, though he is similarly placed.
6.

It is further submitted that the notification under Section 16(2) of the Land Acquisition Act though was issued, only symbolic possession was taken and actual possession was retained with the petitioner.
7. Facts as narrated above are made out from the synopsis filed in Court by learned counsel Sri R.G.Halesha appearing for the petitioner.

8. The learned counsel Sri A.V.Gangadharappa appearing for the respondent, beneficiary of the acquisition, viz., Urban Development Authority, Shivamogga has however contended that the request of the petitioner for dropping the proceedings for acquisition was rejected, that General Award was passed by the Land Acquisition Officer with respect to the entirety of the extent of 7 acres 28 guntas, that possession of lands was taken as evidenced by Section 16(2) notification and the mahazar prepared by the Office of the Tahsildar, that W.P.No.34493/1995 was filed challenging the validity of the acquisition proceedings by the same petitioner which came to be rejected, that petitioner had sought for making of reference to the Civil Court under Section 18 seeking enhancement of compensation, that revenue entries have been entered in the name of the Urban Development Authority after acquisition, that petitioner has accepted compensation for the entirety of the land.

9. Heard both sides.
10.

The question is as to whether the petitioner is entitled for a direction to the Government to consider passing notification, de-notifying the petitioner's land in Survey No.9, measuring 1 acre 28 guntas, taking note of such relief extended by the Government in favour of Sri Madarsab, land owner in Survey No.131 measuring 3 acres 23 guntas and Sri Parameshwarappa, land owner in Survey No.16/2 measuring 1 acre 14 guntas.
11.
At the outset, it must be noted that the question of de-notification would not arise, if possession has been taken.

Section 48(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 provides as follows:-
"48. Completion of acquisition not compulsory, but compensation to be awarded when not completed."

3 1.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Except in the case provided for in Section 36, the Government shall be at liberty to withdraw from the acquisition of any land of which possession has not been taken.
(emphasis supplied)

12. In the present case, Section 16(2) notification under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 has been published in the Gazette on 22.01.1998 and would indicate that the entire extent of 7 acres 28 guntas in Survey No.9 belonging to the petitioner has been taken over on 12.08.2014 (see Annexure-'R3' filed alongwith the statement of objections of respondent No.3 dated 30.07.2014).
13.

Admittedly, the Award has been passed for the entire extent of 7 acres 28 guntas in Survey No.9 (Annexure-R4 filed alongwith I.A. for additional documents dated 02.08.2019) and same has been approved by the Government as per Annexure-'R5'.

As per mahazar at Annexure-'R6' possession has been taken.
14.

As per Annexure-'R10', the Revenue Inspector of the Shivamogga Urban Development Authority (SUDA) has prepared a mahazar which bears the signature of the Revenue Inspector, who makes a observation that lands have been handed over to SUDA by the Government.

The signature of the Revenue Inspector, SUDA is also affixed in the said document with the observation that the possession is being accepted on behalf of the SUDA as has been handed over by the Tahsildar and signature of the witnesses are also found.

15. Admittedly, there is a presumption that would come into play regarding taking over possession and its vesting in the Government free from all encumbrances by virtue of notification passed under Section 16(2) [Karnataka amendment to Section 16].

The provision makes it clear that "such notification shall be evidence of such fact."
16.
As noticed above, there is a notification published in the Gazette regarding the entirety of the extent of 7 acres 28 guntas belonging to the petitioner.

Apart from such notification, the mahazar dated 11.03.1997 prepared in the presence of witnesses having the signature of the Revenue Inspector, who narrates handing over possession on behalf of the Government, which possession is acknowledged by the Revenue Inspector, SUDA would be sufficient evidence of taking over of possession by SUDA from the Government.
The above method adopted for taking over of possession does not call for disbelieving the same.

17. Though learned counsel for the petitioner has disputed the factum of taking possession, no grounds are made out to disbelieve the presumption of the notification under Section 16(2) and the mahazar dated 22.02.1996 and 11.03.1997.
If that were to be so, the question of seeking de-notification would not arise.

18. Insofar as the contention that compensation has not been paid for the entire extent and that compensation has been withdrawn only as regards the extent of 6 acres, is a matter that requires consideration.

sentences.text: The petitioner has referred to Annexure-'F', wherein there is a reference that 1 acre 28 guntas of coconut land has been left out, wherein the extent is shown as 6 acres, Annexure-'G', wherein the extent of land acquired in Survey No.9 is shown as 6 acres.

Reliance is also placed on the order in LAC No.143/1999, wherein the learned Judge while considering the reference under Section 18 for enhancement, has observed that an extent of 6 acres has been acquired out of the extent of 7 acres 28 guntas.
Accordingly, it is submitted that the compensation was only with respect to an extent of 6 acres.

20. While Sri A.V.Gangadharappa on the other hand has drawn attention of the Court to the Award at Annexure-'R4', wherein there is a reference of the Award having been passed for the extent of 7 acres 28 guntas in Survey No.9 and submits that once Award is passed for the entire extent, the compensation that has been paid must be construed as being paid for the entire extent of 7 acres 28 guntas.

Reliance is placed on Memo of Calculations filed in LAC No.143/1999, wherein compensation is calculated with respect to the entire extent of 7 acres 28 guntas in Survey No.9.
21.

Though various contentions have been advanced regarding the compensation, it must be noted that once possession is taken as observed above, the payment or otherwise of compensation for the entire extent, even if it admits ambiguity will not provide any relief to the petitioner, as the only relief sought for is one of de-notification by the Government.
Further, it must be noticed that the petitioner has also not sought for any relief regarding lapse and the only relief for consideration is as regards de-notification.

22. Though the petitioner has sought for similar relief as in W.P.No.5486/2010, in the case of Sri Parameshwarappa, it must be noted that the Court in that matter had recorded a specific finding that possession was not taken on the basis of the records produced (see para-5).
While holding that land not having vested in the Government, it was observed that the State Government ought to have treated Sri Parameshwarappa on same lines as that of Madarsab.

However, in the present case, in light of the specific finding that possession has been taken by reference to the 16(2) notification and the mahazar, relief as made out to Parameshwarappa in W.P.No.5486/2010 cannot be extended to the petitioner herein.
23. While insofar as the case of Madarsab is concerned, his land also has been de
- notified as per the notification dated 15.04.1998 and petitioner states that he stands on parity and requires to be extended similar relief.
It is the contention of learned counsel Sri A.V.Gangadharappa that the land involved was the land used for burial ground and was Wakf land and accordingly, such order was passed.
However, it must be noticed that the Government has rejected the request for de-notification on the ground that possession is taken in terms of the endorsement at Annexures-'K1' and 'N2'.

If that were to be so, the Court cannot compel the Authority to treat the case of the petitioner on parity with Parameshwarappa in whose case the Court has recorded a finding that possession was not taken, or the case of Madarsab.
This is more so, as once possession is taken, the question of de-notification will not arise.
